side.notes: Multiple exact live-fish and voucher pages show a deep, laterally compressed trunk, steep convex predorsal profile, large eye, terminal mouth, fin origins, short peduncle, forked caudal, and bounded posterior axine.

top.uncertainty: High. No verified true dorsal or orthographic top original was found; FishBase calls the cross section compressed and the spawning oblique supports narrow width only qualitatively.
top.notes: Half-width and dorsal outline are retained from the anatomical source controls rather than calibrated to an unavailable top photograph.

front.uncertainty: High. No verified sharp orthographic frontal original was found, and the available spawning image is foreshortened and motion blurred.
front.notes: Frontal head thickness and eye protrusion remain conservative inferences from the compressed classification, lateral head views, and qualitative oblique view.

silhouetteLandmarks.name: steep convex snout-to-predorsal profile and deep trunk
silhouetteLandmarks.notes: Revised station heights hold depth at the dorsal-fin origin near Tan's reported mean while moving maximum depth behind the shortened head, flattening the swollen belly transition, and preserving the steep convex predorsal rise.

silhouetteLandmarks.name: short caudal peduncle and symmetrical forked caudal
silhouetteLandmarks.notes: Peduncle stations narrow rapidly before equal caudal spans and a fork control form the symmetric tail silhouette.

silhouetteLandmarks.name: large eye, short opercular region, and small terminal mouth
silhouetteLandmarks.notes: The shortened head and snout stations retain the terminal mouth, while a smaller, tilted, deeply seated eye preserves the observed large lateral eye without the failed candidate's bead-like protrusion.

silhouetteLandmarks.name: dorsal, pelvic, anal, pectoral, and caudal fin placement
silhouetteLandmarks.notes: Median-fin extents and paired-fin roots map the observed lateral origins without changing unrelated fin geometry.

proportions.name: maximum adult total length
proportions.notes: FishBase reports 5.0 cm maximum total length; the source package records that value directly.

proportions.name: body depth at dorsal-fin origin divided by standard length
proportions.notes: Tan reports 32.6 to 38.2 percent of standard length, mean 35.8 percent, for T. heteromorpha. The revised source evaluates to 35.34 percent at the dorsal-fin origin over the 39 mm station-defined standard length. This source calculation is in range, but the unbuilt candidate still requires visual comparison.

proportions.name: axine anterior depth divided by body depth
proportions.notes: Tan diagnoses the T. heteromorpha axine as more than two-thirds of body depth at its broad anterior end. Independent dorsal and ventral bounds now preserve that local depth while tapering toward the peduncle rather than filling the whole posterior flank.

proportions.name: side-to-side width relative to vertical body depth
proportions.uncertainty: High. This conservative compressed-body ratio is not a published T. heteromorpha measurement and no orthographic top or front source was found.
proportions.notes: FishBase's compressed classification and the spawning oblique support a narrow section qualitatively, but they do not justify a calibrated observed ratio.

colorPatternBoundaries.name: three-apex posterior axine
colorPatternBoundaries.notes: The black field begins with dorsal and ventral apices near their fin origins, has a straight to gently sloped anterior boundary, and narrows to a caudal apex at the caudal-fin base.

colorPatternBoundaries.name: orange-red body sheen and dark dorsal shading
colorPatternBoundaries.notes: Procedural vertical blends keep the warm live-fish body color separate from both the dark dorsum and sharply bounded axine.

colorPatternBoundaries.name: orange-red dorsal with translucent paired and anal fins
colorPatternBoundaries.notes: Fin-type branches control opaque warm dorsal and caudal color separately from the more translucent paired and anal fins.

mismatches.note: The preserved rebuild shows the corrected axine but remains too capsule-like, with a blunt head, swollen belly-to-head transition, protrusive eye, and oversized median fins. The revised lateral stations reduce the anterior and ventral fullness, shorten the head transition, seat the eye, and reduce fin spans. These are source-level resolutions of the known prebuild blockers, not a claim that the unbuilt result has passed visual review.

The original axial tuple [7, 11, 18, 27] first failed Spine_B at quarter phase by 0.7672 degrees. The coordinated tuple [5, 7.5, 12, 17] advanced past earlier failures but exposed Peduncle at half phase by 1.0806 degrees. Shared plan code proves the four values map to Spine_A, Spine_B, Peduncle and Caudal, so reducing only the third value from 12 to 8 predicts 0.7204 degrees under the observed amplitude-linear parity error, leaving 0.0296 degrees margin. A new build must verify the prediction.

Exact width and frontal head shape remain uncertain because no verified orthographic top or frontal original was found. Existing compressed-body controls are retained and explicitly treated as inference.
Fin rays remain normal-map relief rather than individually modeled structures; this representational simplification was not a rejection cause.

failedCandidateEvidence.runtimeError: Parity burst 0.50 Peduncle: 1.0806 degrees with the coordinated [5, 7.5, 12, 17] tuple
failedCandidateEvidence.renderReview: The bounded three-apex axine reads correctly and must remain unchanged. The revised side silhouette, head taper, eye seating, body depth and fin scale passed the required static three-view review; top and front remain explicitly high-uncertainty inferred views.

cueComparison.reference: A straight-edged posterior triangle with dorsal and ventral apices near their fin origins and a caudal apex tapering along the peduncle to the caudal-fin base.
cueComparison.before: The earlier rejected candidate used a U-threshold that filled nearly the full posterior body depth.
cueComparison.afterSourceLogic: The preserved rebuild proves the independent dorsal and ventral bounds form the intended three-apex wedge. This source logic is retained unchanged.

cueComparison.reference: Deep, laterally compressed trunk; steep convex predorsal profile; short peduncle; forked caudal.
cueComparison.before: The preserved rebuild is deep but too uniformly rounded, with excess anterior and ventral fullness that reads as a capsule rather than a compressed cyprinid.
cueComparison.afterSourceLogic: Anterior, opercular, head, and snout depths taper sooner; the belly is reduced more than the predorsal ridge. At the dorsal-fin origin, source depth is 35.34 percent of the station-defined standard length, within Tan's 32.6 to 38.2 percent range.

cueComparison.reference: Large round eye, short opercular region, small terminal mouth, orange-red dorsal, translucent paired fins and forked caudal.
cueComparison.before: The preserved rebuild has a blunt swollen head, a bead-like eye standing proud of the flank, and median and paired fins that dominate the small body.
cueComparison.afterSourceLogic: The head transition and snout are shortened and tapered, eye radius and proud depth are reduced with local-surface seating, and dorsal, anal, caudal, pectoral, and pelvic spans are reduced without changing the diagnostic axine or terminal mouth.

cueComparison.reference: FishBase states a compressed cross section; oblique spawning imagery supports narrow width only qualitatively.
cueComparison.before: The failed three-view is compatible with lateral compression, but no calibrated top reference exists.
cueComparison.afterSourceLogic: Half-width stations and cross-section exponents remain unchanged; no unsupported top-outline or frontal correction is introduced.

parityPrediction.model: With frame count, frequency, lag, envelope, export and importer fixed, quaternion interpolation error at a sampled phase scales approximately with that bone's rotation amplitude. Predictions scale each observed error by afterAmplitude / observedAmplitude.
parityPrediction.rationale: The newest failure is isolated to the third travelling-wave channel, which shared plan code maps to Peduncle. Only that amplitude is reduced, while Spine_A, Spine_B, Caudal, frequency, lag, envelope and non-axial channels remain unchanged. This is a prebuild prediction, not runtime validation.

uncertainty: No verified true dorsal/top or sharp frontal original was found. Width and frontal head shape remain constrained only by the authoritative compressed classification plus qualitative oblique views.
pixelPolicy: No reference pixels were copied, sampled, traced or redistributed.
